towers.name: Pulse Turret
towers.note: Baseline. Cheap to run — the one you leave online during a brownout. Engages air, but only what a scan relay is revealing, so on anchor-02 cutting the relay blinds every gun on the board rather than disarming them.

towers.name: Arc Node
towers.note: Chains. Draw is high enough that two of them force a real decision.

towers.name: Ion Lance
towers.note: Only reliable answer to shielded units. Cannot be left running casually.

towers.name: Shield Wall
towers.note: Slows hard over a wide arc and shoots nothing. Ties the arc node as the biggest draw in Act I, so it is the emplacement most likely to push a tuned bus into overdraw — which is the point. At 40 MW with a 0.45x slow in radius 2.0 it was never worth building (LF-032): a 42% overdraw bought a slow across two tiles of a forty-tile path.

towers.name: Scan Relay
towers.note: Reveals air and shielded units. First thing players learn to cut mid-wave.

towers.name: Flak Array
towers.note: Act II. Bursts over a lane rather than hitting one unit, so it answers the skiff-and-drone packs Sable Reach leads with. Still needs a relay to see air — splash does not find what the board cannot see.

towers.name: Anchor Damper
towers.note: Act II. Suppresses most of the bus drain of anything in range — a fixed 18 MW spent to deny a variable theft. Worth building exactly when the wave carries more drain than the damper costs, which is the decision Act II is made of.

towers.name: Mortar Emplacement
towers.note: Act II. Long reach and a wide burst, but slow and blind to air. Reaches across a board the lance cannot cover twice.
